title: Probing Entanglement Scaling Across a Quantum Phase Transition on a Quantum Computer
abstract: First demonstration of log-law scaling of subsystem entanglement entropies at criticality on a digital quantum computer. Uses MERA circuits on a trapped-ion quantum computer with 15 Yb-171 ions, employing binary 1D MERA with bond dimension chi=2 and up to T=5 layers (12 qubits used). Studies the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) across its quantum phase transition, observing Z2 symmetry breaking in the ferromagnetic phase and universal scaling near the critical point. Classically pre-optimized MERA tensors, symmetry-constrained gate compilation.
key_claims: First log-law entanglement scaling at criticality on quantum hardware
Binary MERA chi=2 up to T=5 layers on 12-qubit trapped-ion system
Symmetry-constrained gate compilation preserves Z2 and time-reversal symmetry
MERA proven free of barren plateaus (cite Barthel-Miao 2025)
All-to-all connectivity of trapped ions simplifies MERA circuit implementation
L=96 critical Ising model probed with just 12 qubits via MERA holographic structure
